items.title: AI agents open 17 million pull requests a month. I built a gate that rejects the ones that lie.
items.summary: The author demonstrates a deterministic Python gate that validates AI‑generated pull requests before they are merged.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a concrete safety net for autonomous agents modifying codebases.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run the gate script against a test PR to see its verification flow.

items.title: A reader found a hole in our AI inbox. Postgres closes it now
items.summary: A race condition allowed AI-generated milestone proposals to be approved against stale data, causing progress values to silently regress. The fix uses a PostgreSQL trigger to stamp the base state and a transactional check to reject stale proposals.
items.why_it_matters: It prevents silent data corruption in approval workflows by ensuring the database rejects changes based on outdated information rather than relying on UI-level checks.
items.next_step_detail: Apply the latest migration from the repo or run ALTER TABLE proposals ADD COLUMN approval_ts TIMESTAMP DEFAULT now();

items.title: Java4Shell: RCE in OpenJDK when processing Base64
items.summary: Disclosure of CVE‑2026‑114938, a critical memory‑corruption RCE in OpenJDK’s Base64 decoder.
items.why_it_matters: If your stack runs Java services (e.g., Spark, Flink) you must patch to avoid remote code execution.
items.next_step_detail: Upgrade OpenJDK to version 21.0.3+ or later where the fix is back‑ported.
items.verification_note: If your stack runs Java services (e.g., Spark, Flink) you must patch to avoid remote code execution.

items.title: usestrix / strix
items.summary: Strix is an open-source AI penetration testing framework that uses autonomous agents to dynamically run code, find vulnerabilities, and validate them with working proofs-of-concept. It integrates with CI/CD pipelines to automatically scan for vulnerabilities on every pull request and block insecure code before it reaches production.
items.why_it_matters: It provides fast, accurate security testing with real exploit validation to avoid the false positives of static analysis tools, while offering remediation guidance and compliance-ready reports.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run `pip install -r requirements.txt && python strix/run.py` against a test service.

items.title: What is the best harness for each model?
items.summary: Runta's FrontierHarness v1.1 evaluates 22 harness configurations across 5 models and 62 tasks to determine the optimal pairing for each model. The results show that the best-value harness changes depending on the model, with specific pairings like Codex CLI with GLM-5.3 or ZCode with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 offering the lowest cost per pass.
items.why_it_matters: The benchmark provides specific data on which harness minimizes cost per pass for each model, addressing the question of whether to switch harnesses when switching models.

items.title: Microsoft's ONNX Runtime has disappeared from GitHub

items.why_it_matters: ONNX Runtime is a core component for serving open‑source LLMs; its disappearance could break inference pipelines.
items.next_step_detail: Monitor the official Microsoft channels for a replacement repo or migration instructions.

items.title: How the Claude Code team thinks about verification

items.title: Thinking On or Off? Gemma 4 E2B on an 8 GB RTX 3050
items.summary: Gemma 4 E2B on an 8 GB RTX 3050 shows that enabling thinking mode doubles inference time without improving GSM8K or AIME scores, while adding a drafter reduces generation time by up to 2.04 times with no change in accuracy. The Q4_0 repack weights are smaller and faster than the original Google QAT build while producing identical results.
items.why_it_matters: The drafter is the only configuration change that consistently improves performance, making it the recommended deployment option for local inference on this hardware.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run the provided benchmark script on your own RTX 3050 or similar GPU.

items.title: Launch HN: StarSling (YC P25) – Self-improving CI for agent-volume repos
items.summary: StarSling offers a CI platform that automatically optimizes pipelines for repositories containing many AI agents, aiming to reduce review and build latency.
items.why_it_matters: It directly addresses the CI bottleneck for teams deploying large numbers of autonomous agents.
items.next_step_detail: Sign up for a free trial at starsling.dev and run it on a sample agent repo.

items.title: HKUDS / RAG-Anything
items.summary: RAG-Anything is an all-in-one multimodal document processing RAG system built on LightRAG that handles text, images, tables, and equations. It provides a unified framework for querying documents with interleaved content types through a single interface.
items.why_it_matters: It eliminates the need for multiple specialized tools by delivering comprehensive multimodal retrieval capabilities for documents containing mixed content.
items.next_step_detail: git clone https://github.com/HKUDS/RAG-Anything && pip install -r requirements.txt

items.title: Harvard researchers find AI coding agents shifted the bottleneck to code review
items.summary: A working paper reports that firms using AI coding assistants produce 30% more code but see a 49% increase in code‑review time, highlighting a new workflow bottleneck.

items.next_step_detail: Read the full working paper to assess how review processes might need redesign.

items.title: HF Paper: Invariant-Aware Harness Enforcement to Protect LLM Agents from Silent API Failures
items.summary: Presents a harness that enforces invariant checks on LLM‑agent API calls, detecting silent failures where APIs return plausible but incorrect results.
items.why_it_matters: Directly improves reliability of your production LLM agents that depend on external services.

items.title: Prompt Regression Testing for LLM Apps: A Free CI Gate, Tested on 3 Real Models
items.summary: A lightweight CI gate runs regression tests on LLM prompts using recorded answers to detect silent behavior changes, demonstrated with Llama 3.2 3B, Qwen 2.5 1.5B, and Gemma 3 1B. The system uses per-case rules to block prompt edits that degrade specific behaviors, such as refund logic, even when overall scores remain stable.
items.why_it_matters: It prevents the merging of prompt changes that silently break critical business rules, such as refund policies, which standard green checks might miss.
items.next_step_detail: Add the provided GitHub Action YAML to your repo and run `git push` to see the gate in action.

items.title: jingyaogong / minimind
items.summary: MiniMind is an open-source project that trains a 64M-parameter language model from scratch in approximately two hours on a single NVIDIA 3090 GPU at a cost of 3 RMB. It provides a complete training pipeline covering pretraining, SFT, LoRA, and RLHF, implemented natively in PyTorch without relying on high-level third-party abstractions.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a reproducible, low-cost environment for understanding LLM internals by implementing core algorithms from zero, rather than relying on abstracted frameworks.
items.next_step_detail: Follow the repo’s quick‑start guide and benchmark training time on your hardware.

items.title: Build a Tiny LLM Output Evaluation Harness in Python (No Framework Required)
